savings.reason: Within the complete original and held full actors EO:13028, EO:13131 and EO:13345, no clause expressly preserves EO:12757 authority after the unconditional section 6(a) revocation. EO:13345 sections 1-5 separately establish successor assignments and Board administration; they do not preserve the old order as a source of authority. This bounded observation does not cure the absent EO:12823 chain text or approve an earliest-ending claim.

research_rationale: The complete held original contains independent Treasury and State functions, Council membership and referral machinery, State agreement and Board obligations, Board membership/officers/duties, a default-conditioned prohibition, and a judicial-review limitation. Exact-span inventory corrections remove the machine preamble clause, page furniture and filing text, and separate the independent reporting and Board-office commands. The section 5 own-term condition excuses particular agreements if the country meets its obligations or the President authorizes; it does not terminate the general rule, and no occurrence facts establish an earlier whole-clause end. EO:13028 section 1 alters delegations and redesignates original section 6 without extinguishing its judicial-review limitation. EO:13131 further changes agreement/Board provisions, including a replacement of section 4(d), which requires comparison against EO:12823 rather than assuming 1999 is the first end of the 1991 four-member rule. EO:13345 section 6(a) says the order is hereby revoked and states no postponed date; the full actor is dated July 8, 2004, while July 13 is publication. That is the outer end bound. The affirmative absent EO:12823 amendment prevents earliest-ending determinations. No hypothetical statutory gap is added. No conflicts are enumerated in the dossier. No machine search is adopted while the known material chain gap remains.
unresolved_material_gaps: EO:12823 is affirmatively identified as an amendment of EO:12757 in the full originals of EO:13028 section 1 and EO:13131 section 1, but its text/provision is absent from this dossier. Its changes must be read to establish the first end of every affected original delegation, Board assignment and other command; the 2004 blanket revocation establishes an outer bound, not the earliest cessation of each original clause.
